children: U.S. high-yield credit
market stress is escalating as risk premiums on the lowest-rated corporate debt reach their highest levels since late 2022, according to The Kobeissi Letter.

Credit spreads for corporate bonds rated CCC and lower have widened to 12%, surpassing the April 2025 peak of 11.4% and hitting their highest mark since November 2022, according to data highlighted by Kobeissi in a social media post.
These spreads have jumped by nearly 300 basis points over the past five months alone, though they remain well below the 19.6% peak recorded during the 2020 pandemic crisis.
While heavily distressed outlier issuers are driving a significant portion of the widening, the pressure is spreading across the broader high-yield universe, Deer Point Macro observed.

The median CCC constituent's spread widened by roughly 66 basis points over the past month, pointing to a cross-sectional repricing that is becoming systematic rather than isolated to a few distressed names.

Moreover, at the individual security level, an increasing number of bonds previously trading between 80 and 90 cents on the dollar have dropped to around 60 cents, signaling broader underlying weakness that warrants close monitoring even as analysts assess whether the shift represents a normalization from historic tights or deeper fundamental stress.
